key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Perennial herb, usually about 10–50 cm tall; several stems arise from a thick rootstalk, with stems ascending to decumbent and often branched from the base.

key_traits.label: Leaf morphology
key_traits.text: Ovate to lanceolate leaves on petioles; margins often conspicuously wavy/undulate; leaf surfaces can be short-hairy, especially along veins.

key_traits.label: Inflorescence
key_traits.text: Lateral/axillary umbels on upper nodes; commonly one cluster per node and often short-peduncled.

key_traits.label: Flower color
key_traits.text: Greenish-white to yellowish, sometimes with cream or pink tones in the corona.

key_traits.label: Gynostegium detail
key_traits.text: Very long, slender corona hoods extend above the stigmatic head and flare or bow outward near their tips; internal horns are present. This hood shape is exceptionally diagnostic.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: At flower level, the very long slender corona hoods rise above the central gynostegium—an unusually strong Texas milkweed character.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Opposite broad leaves with conspicuously wavy margins.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Low, several-stemmed habit with lateral/axillary umbels.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Use a macro view to separate the corona hoods, central gynostegium, and reflexed corolla parts.

key_traits.label: Joey field note
key_traits.text: Joey Santore's South Texas macro photographs make the decisive floral anatomy especially easy to learn: long narrow hoods/corona surrounding the central gynostegium, with the reflexed corolla visible below.
